note: User Registration Password lets visitors set a password on the registration form when email verification is required, and takes over the activation email. It has no dedicated settings page; it alters core's Account settings form (route entity.user.admin_form, /admin/config/people/accounts). All persistent state is the config object user_registrationpassword.settings (registration in {none=NO_VERIFICATION, default=VERIFICATION_DEFAULT, with-pass=VERIFICATION_PASS; default with-pass}, registration_ftll_expire bool, registration_ftll_timeout int seconds default 86400, registration_redirect path, notify.register_confirmation_with_pass) plus user_registrationpassword.mail. It adds token [user:registrationpassword-url], confirm route user_registrationpassword.confirm, and a REST resource at /user/registerpass. Medium cases seed known values into user_registrationpassword.settings; hard cases mutate it, verified against live config. Scripts touch only this module's config (never core user.settings).

evals.prompt: In the Drupal user_registrationpassword module, which config object and key select the registration/verification behaviour, and what are its three allowed values?
evals.expected_output: The config object user_registrationpassword.settings, key 'registration', accepts 'none' (NO_VERIFICATION), 'default' (VERIFICATION_DEFAULT), or 'with-pass' (VERIFICATION_PASS, the shipped default).

evals.prompt: There is no separate settings page for user_registrationpassword. Where do I configure it in Drupal (route and admin path)?
evals.expected_output: It alters core's Account settings form: route entity.user.admin_form at /admin/config/people/accounts.

evals.prompt: Which token does user_registrationpassword add so the activation/confirmation link can be placed in the welcome email, and what route does it point to?
evals.expected_output: The token [user:registrationpassword-url] builds a one-time confirmation URL for route user_registrationpassword.confirm (user/registrationpassword/{uid}/{timestamp}/{hash}).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the live user_registrationpassword configuration and tell me which registration/verification mode is currently active.
evals.expected_output: user_registrationpassword.settings 'registration' is 'default' (VERIFICATION_DEFAULT — verification email first, password set later).

evals.prompt: Read the live user_registrationpassword configuration on this site: is the account activation link set to expire, and after how many seconds?
evals.expected_output: Activation-link expiry is enabled (registration_ftll_expire = true) with registration_ftll_timeout = 3600 seconds.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure user_registrationpassword so that new visitors are NOT required to verify their email and can set their password directly on the registration form (the NO_VERIFICATION mode). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set user_registrationpassword.settings 'registration' to 'none' (drush cset user_registrationpassword.settings registration none, or via the Account settings form radios).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site I want the account activation links from the User Registration Password module to stop working after 2 hours. Please make the activation link expire, with a lifetime of two hours.
evals.expected_output: Set user_registrationpassword.settings registration_ftll_expire = true and registration_ftll_timeout = 7200 (2 hours in seconds).
